extracted.intended_audience: college instructors and faculty designing service-learning, writing-intensive courses (higher education)
extracted.subtask_description: A flexible service-learning model that integrates student direct service with community partners and student-produced grant-writing products in writing-intensive college courses; includes implementation steps, assessment items, and recommendations for sustainability. Intended to guide instructors in designing and running a semester-long grant-writing service project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of a grant-writing goal relevant to the community organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Select a grant-writing goal that is directly relevant to the partner organization's needs and is appropriate for student skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solicit partner goals via an RFP and initial meetings; partners should specify initiatives to be targeted. Design scope so students' contributions are useful to the organization (examples: full short narratives for some partners; modular reusable sections for others). Instructor/institution should vet scope for fit with students' learning objectives and skill level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structured interaction time between students and community organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide scheduled, structured opportunities for students and community partners to interact throughout the semester.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model used three partner classroom visits (initial presentation, midterm assignment meeting with written assignment description, and final draft feedback). Schedule partner visits during class time to facilitate dialogue and reduce communication problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-class and written reflection on the service experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Include reflective activities (in-class discussion and individual written reflection) to help students connect service with course material and personal development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require an individual response paper (1,000–1,250 words) reflecting either on how the project informed understanding of course issues or future academic/career goals. Build regular debriefs and opportunities for students to share service experiences in class.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct service hours with people receiving services
rubrics_metrics.description: Require students to complete hands-on volunteer hours at the partner site to ground grant-writing in real-world experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the CGWP, students volunteered a minimum of 12 hours in the first half of the semester and at least four 3-hour visits; student feedback recommended more hours. Direct service was rated as highly valuable for informing the writing process and connecting course content to real people.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of a request-for-proposals (RFP) and partner vetting
rubrics_metrics.description: Use an RFP process to solicit interested community partners and vet organizations for fit and willingness to engage with students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partner outreach can be coordinated by a community outreach office; RFP responses should describe organizational needs and how first-year students can contribute. Follow up with phone/in-person meetings to screen partners for appropriate goals and engagement level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage community partners in specifying student assignment scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Have partners articulate assignment descriptions that identify specific deliverables students will produce for the organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partners should prepare written assignment descriptions for student groups; instructor should review these descriptions for scope and appropriateness prior to distribution. Partners should be encouraged to define tasks that are useful but within students' skill sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project timeline: first half service, second half research and writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure the semester so early weeks prioritize site volunteer hours and later weeks focus on research and producing grant materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CGWP timeline: first half—minimum volunteer hours (12+); second half—research and collaborative writing. Build in midterm deliverables (e.g., term paper) and checkpoints with partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative student teams with division of labor and peer-editing
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize students into small collaborative teams responsible for producing grant materials, dividing tasks, and conducting peer edits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: teams of seven worked with one partner. Encourage students to divide workload, arrange informal peer-edits, and coordinate drafts. Instructor provided oversight but students handled primary drafting and finalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructor role: planning oversight and facilitation, limited final proofing
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructor should manage logistics, review assignment scope, facilitate communication, and be available for questions while intentionally not over-editing students' final submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructor worked with community outreach staff pre-semester, reviewed partner assignment descriptions, and was available for general questions, but intentionally did not formally proof final grant narratives prior to submission to preserve student ownership and professional consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide research and library instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer students instruction on library databases and methods for searching peer-reviewed literature to support grant research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mid-semester the instructor and a librarian provided an informational session introducing library databases and search strategies to help students find evidence for grant proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include a professional grant-writer workshop
rubrics_metrics.description: Bring in a practicing grant-writer to present practical guidance on following application instructions and basic grant-writing skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guest lecture emphasized following funder instructions (e.g., page limits) and professional practices; students rated this visit as helpful to the grant-writing process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final deliverables and submission standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Define final deliverables (group binder of organization overview + grant materials; submission in partner-requested format) and require professional submission behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students produced a single hard-copy group binder and submitted final materials electronically per partner preference. Emphasize following funder directions (e.g., page limits) because failure to follow instructions can result in non-review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment: use both institutional course evaluation and supplemental service-learning evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect mixed-method evaluation data from students and community partners using standard university assessment instruments and tailored supplemental evaluations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use standard student assessments (e.g., items on writing, discussion, reading) plus a supplementary anonymous evaluation querying value for learning outcomes, process elements, and long-range value. Include both quantitative scales and open-ended qualitative comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student learning outcome criteria to measure
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure perceived increases in understanding of course material, writing skills, argumentation skills, and ability to connect academic content to the real world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental evaluation in CGWP asked students to rate: increased understanding of course material; improvement in writing skills; improvement in argumentation skills; seeing connections between academic content and the real world. Use Likert scales and report means/SDs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process criteria to measure
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether process elements supported student work: direct service hours, classroom visits from partners, working in collaborative teams, and grant-writing workshop usefulness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In CGWP students rated these process items highly; design surveys to capture these specific elements. Use process feedback to refine scheduling and logistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-range value and recommendation metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask students whether project skills are likely to be useful in future classes or after graduation and whether service-learning should be retained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include items measuring expected utility of skills for future coursework and careers, and an overall retention/recommendation item for the course component.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program success measures from community partner perspective
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate partner outcomes: whether student outputs were used by the organization, whether grants were funded using student work, and whether partners want to continue the relationship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect initial partner motivation surveys and one-year follow-ups to document tangible outcomes (e.g., funded grants and totals) and partner interest in continuing partnerships; use these as evidence of program value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure appropriate scope of student tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: Define the appropriate scope of student contributions (full narratives vs. discrete sections) based on partner needs and student skill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partners may request different types of deliverables; instructors and partners should collaborate to match tasks to first-year students' capabilities and learning goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use institutional community outreach infrastructure for sustainability
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage a community outreach office (or similar) to facilitate partner identification, communication, and project administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CGWP relied on the university's Community Outreach Program to issue the RFP, screen partners, assign an intern, and provide oversight. This infrastructure reduces instructor workload and supports sustainability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify logistics and manage expectations to avoid miscommunication
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize first visits carefully, set clear volunteer schedules, and establish communication protocols to prevent miscommunications about times and expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Student feedback highlighted miscommunications about volunteer times as an area for improvement; literature recommends instructor presence at initial meetings to help set realistic timelines and expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate more explicit writing instruction linked to grant-writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide targeted, in-class instruction that links general writing skills and drafting processes to the specifics of grant-writing to strengthen writing outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CGWP student responses suggested neutral perceptions of writing-skill improvement specifically tied to service activities; recommendation is to devote class time to explicitly connect writing instruction to grant tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build reflective and active-learning course design features
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate active learning methods, opportunities for reflection (writing/talking), and hands-on service to create a positive learning climate and increase student engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design features identified in the literature and incorporated in CGWP include active learning, collaborative teams, reflection assignments, and direct contact with service recipients to enhance retention and student outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid common pitfalls and emphasize professionalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Teach students professional behaviors (e.g., following funder directions, meeting partner expectations) and guard against pitfalls like exceeding page limits or poorly organized site visits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use guest practitioners to stress importance of following instructions; highlight real-world consequences to motivate professional standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustainability and resource considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan for initial faculty/institution time investment to identify partners and set up the project; afterward the model should require minimal funding aside from potential transportation costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CGWP is low-cost and largely self-sustaining once partnerships and goals are established; primary cost is upfront planning and coordination.
